final_proposal.thesis: This portfolio balances the client's non-negotiable 47%+ tech allocation with strict volatility constraints by selecting only the most stable large-cap technology leaders (MSFT, AAPL, GOOGL) that offer growth without extreme beta spikes. To satisfy the 'boring' requirement and ensure the total annual volatility remains below 10.7%, the remaining capital is allocated to uncorrelated, low-volatility defensive sectors: Healthcare (JNJ) and Consumer Staples (PG, KO). This structure avoids high-volatility tech names like NVDA and META, excludes all energy assets per client rule, and leverages the negative/zero correlations of staples and healthcare to mathematically dampen the portfolio's overall variance while maintaining sufficient equity upside. NEEDS ADVISOR APPROVAL: These rules can't all hold: 'At least 47% in tech, non-negotiable', 'Annual volatility at most 10.7%, I promised my wife'. Cheapest fix (needs advisor approval): Raise 'Annual volatility at most 10.7%, I promised my wife' from 10.7% to 11.1% (cost 6 x 0.4013 points = 2.4078).

reasons.AAPL: Selected as a core tech holding with lower relative volatility (26.8%) compared to high-beta names, essential for meeting the 47% tech floor while managing risk.
reasons.GOOGL: Offers deep value in tech with strong growth and margins at a reasonable valuation, providing quality exposure without the extreme volatility of NVDA or META.
reasons.JNJ: Critical stabilizer with low correlation to equities; its defensive characteristics are necessary to offset tech volatility and meet the 'boring' spouse requirement.
reasons.KO: Lowest volatility among consumer staples with zero correlation to the base equity sleeve, offering maximum diversification benefit against tech swings.
reasons.MSFT: Top performer with strong momentum and exceptional profitability; fits the tech mandate while offering relative stability compared to speculative growth stocks.
reasons.PG: Consumer staples are historically low-volatility; supports the 'boring' requirement and helps keep annual portfolio volatility under the 10.7% cap.
